rot.maroczy.ideia.teoria.e1: Attack: this is the Maróczy structure, from the Sicilian Defence. White has the pawns on c4 and e4; Black has the d6 pawn and no c-pawn.
rot.maroczy.ideia.teoria.e2: The c4 and e4 pawns watch the d5 square, and the c4 pawn also watches b5. Black cannot easily bring a pawn to those squares.
rot.maroczy.ideia.teoria.e3: So White has space: more squares for the pieces behind the pawns. The price: with no d-pawn, the d3 and d4 squares have only White pieces to defend them.
rot.maroczy.ideia.teoria.l1: The queen goes to d2, next to the e3 bishop, and connects the rooks on the first rank.
rot.maroczy.ideia.teoria.l2: Black trades knights. The side with less space usually trades pieces: fewer pieces are left for the cramped squares.
rot.maroczy.ideia.teoria.l3: The bishop recaptures and stands on d4, facing the g7 bishop.
rot.maroczy.ideia.teoria.l4: The bishop goes to c6 and, together with the f6 knight, attacks the e4 pawn. Only the c3 knight defends it.
rot.maroczy.ideia.teoria.l5: The f-pawn goes to f3 and defends the e4 pawn a second time.
rot.maroczy.ideia.teoria.l6: The pawn goes to a5. Now the White b-pawn cannot reach b4 without being captured: no pawn will be able to drive a Black knight from c5, where it eyes d3.
rot.maroczy.ideia.teoria.l7: Black forced no advance against the c4 and e4 pawns: they prepared their pieces. In positions like this, White squeezes with the space, and Black waits for the moment of the break.
rot.maroczy.ideia.ourico.e1: Attack: White again, now in the Hedgehog, from the English Opening. The Black pawns on a6, b6, d6 and e6 all stay on the sixth rank.
rot.maroczy.ideia.ourico.e2: Like the spines of a hedgehog, they watch the squares of the fifth rank. Black waits, with the break by the b-pawn or the d-pawn ready for the right moment.
rot.maroczy.ideia.ourico.l1: The e-pawn goes to e4. Now the c4 and e4 pawns watch the d5 square, as in the Maróczy.
rot.maroczy.ideia.ourico.l2: The rook goes to c8, on the half-open c-file, facing the c4 pawn.
rot.maroczy.ideia.ourico.l3: The bishop goes to a3 and attacks the d6 pawn.
rot.maroczy.ideia.ourico.l4: The knight goes to c5: it closes the bishop's diagonal and attacks the e4 pawn.
rot.maroczy.ideia.ourico.l5: The Black pawns stay on the sixth rank, and the pieces defend what is attacked. In positions like this, Black waits for the moment when advancing a pawn wins something.
rot.maroczy.ideia.avanco.e1: Attack: now let us think from Black's side, in a game played on Lichess. It is a Hedgehog: your pawns on a6, b6, d6 and e6 are on the sixth rank.
rot.maroczy.ideia.avanco.e2: The White knight on d4 is within reach of the e6 pawn, if it advances. Further back, on the third rank, are the queen on d3 and the knight on f3.
rot.maroczy.ideia.avanco.p: Find the pawn advance that wins material.
rot.maroczy.ideia.avanco.certo: The pawn advances to e5 and attacks the d4 knight. It will have to move, and the pawn can go on to e4.
rot.maroczy.ideia.avanco.revela: The pawn advances to e5 and attacks the d4 knight: it will have to move, and the pawn will go on to e4.
rot.maroczy.ideia.avanco.fora: That move does not attack the d4 knight. Use a pawn from the sixth rank.
rot.maroczy.ideia.avanco.volta: Try again: attack the d4 knight with a pawn.
rot.maroczy.ideia.avanco.err.d6d5.1: The d6 pawn advances to d5: it is the Hedgehog break, but here it attacks no piece.
rot.maroczy.ideia.avanco.err.d6d5.2: The f3 knight goes to d2 and defends the c4 pawn. The position is equal.
rot.maroczy.ideia.avanco.err.d6d5.3: Back to the position: the e6 pawn has an advance that attacks a piece.
rot.maroczy.ideia.avanco.err.c8c7.1: The rook goes to c7, but it attacks nothing, and White has time.
rot.maroczy.ideia.avanco.err.c8c7.2: The d4 knight goes to e2 and leaves the reach of the e6 pawn.
rot.maroczy.ideia.avanco.err.c8c7.3: Back to the position: attack the d4 knight with a pawn.
rot.maroczy.ideia.avanco.err.b7e4.1: The queen goes to e4 and offers the trade, but it wins nothing.
rot.maroczy.ideia.avanco.err.b7e4.2: The White queen captures yours. After the recapture, the position is equal.
rot.maroczy.ideia.avanco.err.b7e4.3: Back to the position: one of your pawns has an advance that attacks a piece.
rot.maroczy.ideia.avanco.l0: Now White must save the knight.
rot.maroczy.ideia.avanco.l1: The knight goes to f5, from where it attacks the e7 bishop and the d6 pawn.
rot.maroczy.ideia.avanco.l2: The pawn advances to e4 and attacks the d3 queen and the f3 knight at the same time.
rot.maroczy.ideia.avanco.l3: White cannot save both pieces and loses one. In positions like this, the Hedgehog's waiting ends when a pawn advance wins something.
rot.maroczy.demos.regra.1: Attack demonstration: White again, in a game played on Lichess. The Black pawns on a6, b6, d6 and e6 form a Hedgehog, facing yours on b4, c4 and e4.
rot.maroczy.demos.regra.2: The Black queen is on e5, in the centre. Your pawns on b4, c4, e4 and f3 take many squares away from her.
rot.maroczy.demos.regra.l.3: The bishop goes to d4 and attacks the queen. The d2 queen and the b3 knight defend it.
rot.maroczy.demos.regra.l.4: Every square the queen can go to is attacked by a White piece. She captures the bishop, with check, to take something.
rot.maroczy.demos.regra.l.5: The knight recaptures: White gave the bishop and won the queen.
rot.maroczy.demos.regra.l.6: The space of the White pawns left the queen without squares. In positions like this, White squeezes: every watched square is one less square for the Black pieces.
rot.maroczy.demos.regra2.1: Attack demonstration: now let us think from Black's side, in another Lichess game. It is a Maróczy, and the White knight has occupied the d5 square.
rot.maroczy.demos.regra2.2: The c4 and e4 pawns defend the d5 knight. Your f6 knight attacks it and, at the same time, blocks the diagonal of the g7 bishop to the a1 rook.
rot.maroczy.demos.regra2.l.3: The knight captures on d5 and leaves the diagonal: the g7 bishop now attacks the a1 rook.
rot.maroczy.demos.regra2.l.4: The e4 pawn recaptures. If White saved the rook, they would be a knight down.
rot.maroczy.demos.regra2.l.5: The bishop captures the a1 rook.
rot.maroczy.demos.regra2.l.6: Black traded off the strong d5 knight and won a rook. In positions like this, before capturing on d5, check what the trade opens.
rot.maroczy.demos.alvo.1: Attack demonstration: back to the Hedgehog of the first stage, with White, just after the Black rook went to c8 and the White bishop went to a3.
rot.maroczy.demos.alvo.2: The d6 pawn is attacked by the a3 bishop and the d4 queen. The d7 knight blocks the d-file for the Black queen.
rot.maroczy.demos.alvo.l.3: This time Black castles and does not look after the pawn: it is left with one defender, the e7 bishop.
rot.maroczy.demos.alvo.l.4: The bishop captures the d6 pawn.
rot.maroczy.demos.alvo.l.6: The queen recaptures. It was two attackers against one defender, and White won the pawn.
rot.maroczy.demos.alvo.l.7: In positions like this, the d6 pawn is White's target: when the attackers outnumber the defenders, it falls.
rot.maroczy.demos.excecao.1: Attack demonstration: Black again, in another Lichess game. White has the c4 and e4 pawns, and the c6 knight attacks your queen and the b8 rook.
rot.maroczy.demos.excecao.2: Your b8 rook attacks the b3 queen, which no piece defends. Your a5 queen attacks the e1 rook.
rot.maroczy.demos.excecao.l.3: The queen captures the e1 rook with check.
rot.maroczy.demos.excecao.l.4: The b1 rook recaptures the queen. If the king ran, Black would stay a rook up.
rot.maroczy.demos.excecao.l.5: The b8 rook captures the b3 queen.
rot.maroczy.demos.excecao.l.6: Black won a rook: the check came before the plan. In positions like this, before the breaks, look at the checks: a check can win material or even give mate.
rot.maroczy.pratica.valeAqui.enunciado: The Black pawns on a6, b6, d6 and e6 stand on the sixth rank, as in the Hedgehog, and your pieces are close to the Black king. Is it worth thinking about the breaks here? Play as White and find the best move.
rot.maroczy.pratica.valeAqui.fim: The queen gave check on f7, and the king went to h8. The queen entered g7, defended by the g3 rook: it is mate. The attack on the king decided before any pawn plan.
rot.maroczy.pratica.valeAqui.err.h5g5: 24.Qg5? The queen threatens mate on g7, but 24...Ng6 closes the g-file and, by leaving e7, opens the diagonal of the d8 queen to your queen.
rot.maroczy.pratica.valeAqui.err2.h4g6: 25.Ng6+? The knight gives check, but 25...Nxg6 captures it and closes the g-file: the mate is gone. Your queen has a move that ends the game.
rot.maroczy.pratica.avanco.enunciado: It is a Maróczy: the White pawns on c4 and e4 against your d6 pawn. Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.maroczy.pratica.avanco.fim: The pawn advanced to e5 and attacked the d4 knight and the f4 bishop at the same time. The bishop went to e3, and the pawn captured the knight: Black won a piece.
rot.maroczy.pratica.avanco.err.b8d7: 13...Nbd7? The knight comes into play, but the moment passes: your e6 pawn had an advance that attacked two pieces.
rot.maroczy.pratica.avanco.err.a7a6: 13...a6? The pawn prepares the b-pawn advance, but the moment passes: your e6 pawn had an advance that attacked two pieces.
rot.maroczy.pratica.avanco.err.b8c6: 13...Nc6? The knight attacks the d4 knight, but 14.Nxc6 trades it, and the double attack is lost. Your e6 pawn had an advance that attacked two pieces.
rot.maroczy.pratica.casa.enunciado: Black has no c-pawn and no e-pawn. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.maroczy.pratica.casa.fim: The knight entered the d5 square with check and attacked the b6 queen at the same time. The king went to f8, and the knight captured the queen.
rot.maroczy.pratica.casa.err.f4g6: 20.Nxg6+? The knight captures the g6 bishop with check, but 20...fxg6 recaptures, and Black stays better. Your knight has a square from which it attacks two pieces.
